newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI SAYS LINESMAN FIRED OVER FOOTFAULT CALL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI SAYS LINESMAN FIRED OVER FOOTFAULT CALL.

text.p: A linesman who foot-faulted England's Greg Rusedski at match point in the final against Goran Ivanisevic was told by the ATP he will never work another ATP tournament again, Rusedski said Friday.
"It was a Croatian individual who will never work again," said Rusedski, who lost the match (8-6) to the Croatian Ivanisevic in Zagreb on February 2.
After the linesman foot-faulted him on match point, "the supervisor put in the word to kick him out," Rusedski said.
It is extremely rare for foot faults to be called on a match point.
An ATP official at the $303,000 Sybase Open in San Jose, California, where Rusedski is playing, denied that Darby made such a move.
Rusedski, who upset Michael Chang Friday to reach the Sybase Open semifinals, said chair umpire Rudi Berger, who is not allowed to overrule foot faults, and Ivanisevic, were surprised at the call.
"I think Goran was shocked," Rusedski said. "Rudi felt bad, but he couldn't do anything ... The only two foot faults called against me in the match were in the tiebreaker."
Rusedski said although he feels a he was victimised he is ready to move on.

"Obviously you feel like that but you take it as a positive week," he said. "I beat (Thomas) Enqvist and (Jan) Siemerink who I have a losing record against, so I decided to come to San Jose and keep going.
"If you let those little setbacks in life get you down, you are not looking at the big picture."
